zh: 要会的那个要紧人姓古，广东人，是个“通事”，结交的洋朋友极多，对英国人尤其熟悉，而在上海的英国人，自从洪秀全在江宁开国，便有许多花样。他们去会那姓古的，就是要打听这些花样。尤五在上海的路子也很广，辗转打听到，英国洋行已经跟洪军展开贸易。曾经有两只英国兵船，从上海开到下关。洪军起初以为是清军邀来助阵的，大起戒备。谁知英国人带了一名通事上岸，一开口就表明，此来特为通商。商品是枪械火药，以货易货。那家洋行，大获其利，而所带的通事，就是这个姓古的，名叫古应春。
en: The important man they were to meet was a Cantonese interpreter named Gu. He had many foreign friends and was particularly familiar with the British. Since Hong Xiuquan had established his kingdom at Jiangning, the British in Shanghai had been trying all manner of schemes. It was these schemes that Hu and You wanted to learn about. You Laowu had extensive connections in Shanghai, and through a succession of inquiries he had discovered that a British firm was already trading with Hong’s army. Two British warships had sailed from Shanghai to Xiaguan. At first the rebels had assumed that the Qing forces had invited them to help fight, and had taken elaborate precautions. But the British had brought an interpreter ashore, and his opening words made it clear that they had come expressly to trade. Their merchandise consisted of firearms and gunpowder, to be exchanged for other goods. The firm had made a handsome profit. The interpreter who had accompanied them was this very man, Gu Yingchun.

zh: 于是胡雪岩又有了新的主意，他跟尤五商量，最好能够跟古应春结交，在珍宝和枪械方面都有生意好做。尤五对胡雪岩已到了言听计从的地步，便设法托人，从中介绍，前一天已在吃花酒的场面上见过面，当时约定，这天是尤五回请，全班人马，一个不缺，其实主客只有一个古应春。设席的地点在宝善街怡情院。尤五是这家“长三堂子”的主政，怡情老二的恩客，所以连带胡雪宕亦有宾至如归之乐。到了那里，在“大房间”落座，刚刚卸去长衫，听“相帮”在喊客到，怡情老二亲自打开帘子，只见古应春步履轻快地踏上台阶了。“古大少，真真够交情。”怡情老二盈盈笑着，“第一个到。”“尤五哥请客不能不早点来。”古应春又说，“而且是在你这里请客，更不能不早到。”“这是我沾尤五少的光，谢谢，谢谢！”
en: This gave Hu Xueyan another idea. He told You that they ought to make Gu’s acquaintance: there would be business to do in both precious objects and arms. By now You followed Hu’s advice in everything. He arranged an introduction through a mutual acquaintance, and the previous day they had met over a banquet with courtesans. It had been agreed then that You would return the hospitality today, with the entire party invited again. In reality, there was only one guest who mattered: Gu Yingchun. The dinner was to be held at Yiqing House on Baoshan Street, an establishment of the prestigious changsan class. You was a favored patron of Yiqing’s Second Miss, the woman who ran the house, so Hu too enjoyed the pleasure of being received as one of the household. They had scarcely taken their seats in the main room and removed their long gowns when an attendant called out that a guest had arrived. Second Miss herself lifted the curtain, revealing Gu Yingchun coming briskly up the steps. “Young Master Gu, you really do honor your friends!” she said with a graceful smile. “The very first to arrive.” “When Brother You gives a dinner, I can hardly be late,” Gu replied. “And when he gives it at your house, I must certainly come early.” “Then I owe this honor to Fifth Master You. Thank you, thank you!”

zh: “承情之至。”尤五也拱手致谢，接着向里一指，“要不要里头躺一会？”“我是过足了瘾来的。不过躺一会也可以。”一听这话，怡情老二便喊：“点灯！”接着把古应春的哔叽袍子接过来，引入里间。里间就是怡情老二的香闺，一色红木家具，却配了一张外国来的大铜床，雪白珠罗纱的帐子吊得高高地，床上已设着一副极精致的鸦片烟具。古应春略略客气了一下，先在上首躺下，对面的空位，尤五让胡雪岩，胡雪岩又让尤五，这是一番做作，胡雪岩是客，而且有话要问古应春，自然该他相陪。
en: “Much obliged,” You said, clasping his hands in thanks. Then he gestured toward the inner room. “Would you like to lie down for a while?” “I had my fill of opium before coming, but I wouldn’t mind lying down.” At this, Second Miss called, “Light the lamp!” She took Gu’s serge gown and led him inside. The inner room was her own bedchamber. Its furniture was all of rosewood, except for a large imported brass bed, whose snowy gauze curtains were drawn high. An exquisite set of opium implements had already been laid out on it. After a token show of reluctance, Gu reclined in the place of honor. You offered the opposite place to Hu, and Hu offered it back to You. These were formalities. Hu was the guest, and he had questions for Gu; naturally, he was the one to keep him company.

zh: “香”过两筒烟，说过一番闲话，怡情老二要去招呼“台面”，尤五也另有客要陪，小屋间里便只剩下胡、古二人。胡雪岩已经看出，古应春也是个很“外场”的人物，不难对付，因而一上来便用请教的口气说：“应春兄，我总算运气不错，夷场上得有识途老马指点，以后要请你多多指教。”“不敢当。”古应春笑道，“尤五哥是我久已慕名的，他对你老兄特别推重，由此可见，足下必是个好朋友，我们以后要多亲近。”“是，是！四海之内皆弟兄，况且海禁已开，我们自己不亲近，更难对付洋人了。”“着！”古应春拿手指拍着烟盘，“雪岩兄，你这话真通达。说实在的、我们中国人，就是自己弄死自己，白白便宜洋人。”
en: After two pipefuls and some idle conversation, Second Miss went out to attend to the dinner, while You had other guests to entertain. Hu and Gu were left alone. Hu had already seen that Gu was a man well accustomed to society and would be easy to approach. He began in the tone of one seeking guidance. “Brother Yingchun, I count myself fortunate to have found an old hand to show me the way in the foreign settlement. I shall often have to ask your advice.” “You flatter me,” Gu said with a smile. “I have admired Brother You’s reputation for a long time. He speaks very highly of you, which tells me that you must be a friend worth having. We ought to see more of each other.” “Indeed! All men within the four seas are brothers. And now that the maritime prohibitions have been lifted, it will be harder still to deal with the foreigners unless we Chinese stick together.” “Exactly!” Gu tapped the opium tray with a finger. “Brother Xueyan, that is a thoroughly sensible remark. The truth is that we Chinese ruin one another and let the foreigners reap the benefit.”

zh: 这话就有意思了，胡雪岩心想，出言要谨慎，可以把他的话套出来。“现在新兴出来‘洋务’这两个字，官场上凡是漂亮人物，都会‘谈洋务’，最吃香的也是‘办洋务’，这些漂亮人物我见过不少，象应春兄你刚才这两句话，我却还是第一次听见。”“哼！”古应春冷笑着，对胡雪岩口中的“漂亮人物”，做了个鄙夷不屑的表情。“那些人是闭门造车谈洋务，一种是开口就是‘夷人’，把人家看做茹毛饮血的野人，再一种是听见‘洋人’二字，就恨不得先跪下来叫一声：”洋大人‘。这样子谈洋务、办洋务，无非自取其辱。““这话透彻得很。”胡雪岩把话绕回原来的话头上，“过与不及，就‘自己人弄死自己人’了。”“对了！”古应春拿烟签子在烟盘上比划着说：“恨洋人的，事事掣肘，怕洋人的，一味讨好，自己互相倾轧排挤，洋人脑筋快得很，有机可乘，决不会放过。这类人尤其可恶。”
en: There was something in that remark. Hu decided that, with a little care, he could draw Gu out. “These days everyone talks about ‘foreign affairs.’ All the fashionable figures in official circles discuss foreign affairs, and managing them is the most sought-after occupation of all. I have met plenty of those gentlemen, but this is the first time I have heard anyone say what you have just said.” “Hmph!” Gu gave a contemptuous smile at Hu’s mention of these fashionable figures. “They discuss foreign affairs shut up in their own rooms, knowing nothing of the world outside. One sort calls foreigners barbarians and treats them as savages who eat raw flesh and drink blood. The other can scarcely hear the word ‘foreigner’ without wanting to fall on his knees and cry, ‘Your Excellency!’ Discussing and managing foreign affairs in that spirit brings nothing but humiliation upon ourselves.” “You put it very clearly,” Hu said, steering the talk back to its original point. “Both extremes end in our own people ruining one another.” “Precisely!” Gu gestured over the tray with his opium pick. “Those who hate foreigners obstruct everything; those who fear them do nothing but curry favor. Meanwhile, we undermine and push out our own people. Foreigners are quick to see an opening, and they never let one slip. People of that sort are especially detestable.”

zh: 胡雪岩看他那愤慨的神情，知道他必是受过排挤，有感而发。“不遭人妒是庸才”，受倾轧排挤的人，大致能干的居多，看他说话，有条有理，见解亦颇深远，可以想见其人。于是胡雪岩心想，自己正缺少帮手，尤其是这方面的人才，倘或古应春能为己所用，岂不大妙？这个念头，几乎在他心里一出现，就已决定，但却不宜操之过急，想了想，他提出一个自信一定可以引起古应春兴趣的话题。“应春兄！”他矍然而起，从果碟子，抓了几粒杏仁放在嘴里大嚼，嘴唇动得起劲，说话便似乎格外显得有力，“我有点不大服气！我们自己人弄死自己人，叫洋人占了便宜，难道就不能自己人齐心一致，从洋人手里再把便宜占回来？”古应春听了他的话，只是翻眼，一要烟签子不断在烟盘戳着，好久，他说，“雪岩兄，从来没有人跟我说过这话。上次开了两条兵轮到下关去卖军火，价钱已经谈好，要成交了，有个王八蛋跑来见洋人，他会说洋文，直接告诉洋人，说洪军急需洋枪火药，多的是金银珠宝。说这句话，洋人翻悔了，重新议价，涨了一倍还不止。这就是洋人占的大便宜！我也一直不服气。能够把洋人的便宜占回来，哪怕我没有好处也干。于今照你所说，自己人要齐心一致，这句话要怎么样才能做到，我要请教。“
en: His indignation convinced Hu that he had himself been pushed aside and was speaking from experience. Only a mediocrity escaped envy; those who suffered from rivalry and exclusion were generally capable men. Gu spoke coherently, and his views showed considerable foresight. Hu felt that he could judge the man from his conversation. He was short of helpers, particularly of men with this kind of ability. How useful it would be to bring Gu into his service! The thought had scarcely occurred to him before he resolved to act on it, though he must not be too hasty. After a moment’s reflection, he raised a subject he felt certain would interest Gu. “Brother Yingchun!” He suddenly sat up, took a few almonds from a dish and chewed vigorously, which seemed to give his words added force. “There is something I cannot accept. If we ruin one another and let the foreigners gain at our expense, why can’t we unite and win the advantage back?” Gu looked up, poking repeatedly at the tray with his opium pick. At length he said, “Brother Xueyan, no one has ever said that to me before. The last time we took those two warships to Xiaguan to sell arms, the price had been settled and the bargain was almost concluded when a bastard who spoke their language came to see the foreigners. He told them directly that Hong’s army desperately needed guns and powder and had gold, silver and jewels in abundance. That was enough. The foreigners went back on their word, reopened negotiations and more than doubled the price. What a windfall they made! I have resented it ever since. If I could win that advantage back from them, I would do it even without a profit for myself. But you say our own people must unite. How are we to accomplish that? I should like your advice.”

zh: “这话倒是把我问倒了。”胡雪岩说，“事情是要谈出来的，现在我还不大知道洋人的情形，说不出个所以然来。不过既说齐心一致，总要有个起头。譬如说，你、我，还有尤五哥，三个人在一起，至诚相见，遇事商量，哪个的主意好，照哪个的做，就象自己出的主意一样，这样子一步一步把人拉拢来，洋人不跟我们打交道则已，要打，就非听我们的话不可！”“好！”古应春也一仰身坐了起来：“三人同心、其利断金。就从你、我、尤五哥起头。我洋行里那个‘康白度’也不要做了。”洋行里管事的人叫“康白度”，是洋文的译音，地位又非仅仅负传译之责的通事可比。胡雪岩觉得他不须如此做法。“应春兄，”胡雪岩首先声明：“自己人说话，不妨老实。你洋行里的职位，仍旧要维持，不然跟洋人打交道不方便、而且这一来，洋人那里的消息也隔膜了。”古应春原是不假思索，想到就说的一句话，即使胡雪岩不点明，他回想一下，也会改变主意的。因而当然一迭连声的表示同意。
en: “Now you have put me on the spot,” Hu said. “Things have to be worked out through discussion. I know too little about the foreigners yet to offer a definite answer. Still, if we are to unite, we must make a beginning. Take you, me and Brother You: the three of us could deal with one another in complete sincerity and consult over everything. Whoever has the best idea, we follow it as readily as if it were our own. Then we bring more people together, step by step. The foreigners need not deal with us, but if they do, they will have to listen to us.” “Excellent!” Gu sat up too. “When three men are of one mind, their strength can cut through metal. Let it begin with you, me and Brother You. I’ll give up my job as comprador at the foreign firm.” Comprador was a foreign term for the man who managed a foreign firm’s business dealings. His position stood well above that of an interpreter responsible merely for translating. Hu saw no need for Gu to resign. “Brother Yingchun, between ourselves we should speak frankly. You ought to keep your position at the firm. Otherwise our dealings with foreigners would become inconvenient, and we would lose touch with what was happening among them.” Gu had spoken on impulse. Even without Hu’s reminder, a moment’s reflection would have made him change his mind. Naturally, he agreed at once and repeatedly.

zh: “我在想，”胡雪岩踌躇满志的说，“你刚才所说的‘三人同心，其利断金’。这句话真正不假。我们三个人，各占一门，你是洋行方面，尤五哥是江湖上，我在官场中也还有点路子。这三方面一凑，有得混了！”古应春想一想，果然！受了胡雪岩的鼓舞，他也很起劲的说，“真的，巧得很！这三方面要凑在一起，说实在的，真还不大容易。我们明天好好谈一谈，想些也众不同的花样出来，大大做它一番市面。“因为有此契合，这顿花酒，吃得十分痛快，尤五的手面很大，请的客又都是场面上人，每人都叫了两三个局，莺莺燕燕，此去彼来，弦管嗷嘈，热闹非凡。吃到九点多钟，又有人“翻台”，一直闹到子夜过后，才回裕记丝栈。七姑奶奶和阿珠都已累了一天，早早入梦，老张是一向早睡早起，只有陈世龙一个人，泡了一壶好茶在等他们。
en: “I was thinking,” Hu said with satisfaction, “how true your saying is about three men of one mind cutting through metal. Each of us has his own field: you have the foreign firms, Brother You the brotherhood world, and I have a few connections in official circles. Put those three together and we ought to get somewhere!” Gu considered this and saw that it was so. Encouraged by Hu, he replied enthusiastically, “Indeed! What a fortunate combination. Bringing those three fields together is no easy matter. Let’s have a proper talk tomorrow, think of something different from everyone else and do some business on a grand scale.” Their understanding made the evening’s entertainment especially enjoyable. You was a generous host, and his guests were all men of the world. Each summoned two or three courtesans; the women came and went amid a clamor of strings and pipes. After nine, someone ordered another round of entertainment, and the festivities continued past midnight. When Hu and You returned to Yuji Silk Warehouse, the Seventh Lady and A’zhu, tired by the day’s events, were already asleep. Old Zhang always went to bed and rose early. Only Chen Shilong was waiting, with a pot of good tea ready for them.

zh: “五哥，你困不困？”胡雪岩兴致勃勃的问。“不困。”尤五问道：“你有啥事情要谈？”“事情很多。”胡雪岩转脸说道：“世龙，你也一起听听，我今天替你找了个读洋文的先生。”这一说，尤五立即明白：“你是说古应春！你们谈得怎么样？”“谈得再好都没有了……”胡雪岩把他跟古应春在烟榻上的那一席对话，源源本本地说了给尤五听。尤五比较深沉，喜怒不大形于颜色，但就算如此，也可以发现他眉目轩豁，这几天来阴沉沉的脸色，似乎悄然消失了。“你的脑筋快，”他用徐缓而郑重的声音说，“倒想想看，跟他有什么事可以做联手的。”
en: “Brother You, are you sleepy?” Hu asked eagerly. “Not at all. What do you want to talk about?” “A great many things.” Hu turned to Chen. “Shilong, you should listen too. I found you a teacher of the foreigners’ language today.” You understood at once. “You mean Gu Yingchun! How did your talk go?” “It couldn’t have gone better.” Hu recounted their conversation on the opium couch from beginning to end. You was a reserved man who seldom showed his feelings, but even so, his features visibly brightened. The gloom of the past few days seemed quietly to have lifted. “You have a quick mind,” he said slowly and earnestly. “Think what sort of business we could do together with him.”

zh: “眼前就有一样，不过……”胡雪岩的尾音拖得很长。“咦！”尤五诧异了，“有啥为难的话，说不出口？”“我不晓得你跟卯金刀，到底有没有交情？”“卯金刀”是指刘丽川，尤五当然明白，很快地答了句：“谈不上。”“我这么在想，英国人反正做生意，枪炮可以卖给太平军，当然也可以卖给官军。今天我在席面上听说，两江总督和江苏巡抚，郡为了卯金刀在伤脑筋，奏报出去，轻描淡写，好象是地方上闹事，其实是想多派兵，一仗把他打倒。既然如此，枪炮、火药是要紧的，我们好不好先替他们办个‘粮台’，等他们的兵一到，就好出队打仗。如果你认为这个办法可以，我马上到苏州去跑一趟，江苏巡抚许乃钊是我们杭州人，一定可以找得到路子见一见他。”
en: “There is one opportunity before us already, only…” Hu let the last word linger. “Why, what is so difficult that you can’t say it?” You asked in surprise. “I don’t know whether you have any friendship with ‘Mao, Metal and Knife.’” This was a coded way of writing the surname Liu and referred to Liu Lichuan. You understood immediately. “Nothing worth mentioning.” “Here is what I was thinking. The British are in business, after all. If they can sell guns and cannon to the Taiping forces, they can surely sell them to the government army. I heard at dinner that both the governor-general of Liangjiang and the governor of Jiangsu are worrying over Liu. Their reports play the affair down as a local disturbance, but in reality they mean to send in a large force and crush him in one battle. In that case, guns and powder will be essential. Could we establish a supply office for them in advance, so that when their troops arrive they can go straight into action? If you approve, I’ll go to Suzhou at once. Governor Xu Naizhao of Jiangsu is a fellow Hangzhou man. I can certainly find a way to see him.”

zh: “主意倒是不错。不过我不能做。”“是因为‘圈吉’的关系？”胡雪岩问。“圈吉”周，是指周立春，尤五点点头说，“一点不错，不过你跟他没有交情，你可以做。”“那就算了。第一，要做，就是大家一起来，第二，人家也晓得我跟你的交情，如果你觉得有妨碍，我做了一样也有妨碍。”尤五听得这话，大感快慰，他心里是巴不得胡雪岩不要做，但“光棍不断财路”，明明是笔好生意，自己不能叫他罢手，所以那样言不由衷地说“你可以做”。
en: “The idea is good enough. But I can’t take part.” “Because of ‘Ji in a Box’?” Hu asked. The character ji enclosed in a frame made the surname Zhou: he meant Zhou Lichun. You nodded. “Exactly. But you have no ties to him. You could do it.” “Then let it drop. First, whatever we do, we do together. Second, people know how close we are. If it would put you in a difficult position, my doing it would cause the same difficulty.” You was deeply relieved to hear this. In his heart he had wanted Hu to abandon the scheme, but a man of the brotherhood did not cut off another man’s livelihood. It was plainly a profitable venture; he could not ask Hu to give it up. That was why he had said, against his own wishes, “You could do it.”

zh: “我还有第二条路子，浙江现在正在办团练，湖州由一位姓赵，名叫赵景贤的绅士出面，此人极其通达能干，跟王雪公的公谊私交都不错，我一说就可以成功。”“那好！这笔军火生意，我们一起来做。”“就有一样麻烦，要尤五哥你有办法才能成功。”胡雪岩说，“英国人的兵船开不到湖州，只能在上海交货，上海运到湖州，路上怕有危险。抢掉了怎么办？”“危险也不过上海到嘉兴这一段，一进浙江境界，有官兵护送，哪个敢抢？至于这一段路，归我保险。”尤五又说，“反正我们漕帮弟兄现在都空在那里，要人要船都现成。借此让他们赚一笔水脚，事情再好都没有了。”“这一说，在我们两个人就算定局了。说做就做，你倒再想想看，你那面还有什么事要我做到的？”尤五仔细想了想说，“你请浙江方面，替我们这里的督粮道来封公事，说要用松江漕帮的船运军火。这样，我对官面上就算有了交代。”
en: “There is another course,” Hu continued. “Zhejiang is organizing militia forces. In Huzhou, a gentleman named Zhao Jingxian has taken the lead. He is an exceptionally capable, broad-minded man, and is on good terms with Prefect Wang both publicly and privately. A word from me should settle it.” “Good! Let’s undertake that arms business together.” “There is just one difficulty, and it will depend on you to solve it. British warships cannot reach Huzhou, so delivery would have to be made in Shanghai. The journey from Shanghai to Huzhou might be dangerous. What if the cargo were seized?” “The only dangerous stretch is between Shanghai and Jiaxing. Once it enters Zhejiang, government troops can escort it. Who would dare attack it then? As for the first stretch, I’ll guarantee its safety. Our grain-transport brothers are all idle now, with men and boats ready to hand. Giving them a chance to earn some freight money would be the best possible arrangement.” “Then as far as the two of us are concerned, it is settled. Let’s get on with it. Think again: is there anything else you need me to arrange?” You considered carefully. “Have the Zhejiang authorities send an official letter to our grain transport circuit intendant here, saying that they wish to use the Songjiang grain boats to carry arms. That will put my dealings with the authorities in order.”

zh: “这一定办得到。”胡雪岩转脸对陈世龙说，“又要你辛苦跑一趟了。”“到杭州，还是到湖州？”“先到杭州。如果王大老爷已经回任，你就再到湖州，寻着他算数。不错，”胡雪岩忽然又说，“你正好把阿珠送了回去。”“好的。啥时候走？”“最多两三天，等我在这里接好头，写了信，马上就走。”
en: “That can certainly be done.” Hu turned to Chen. “I’m afraid I must send you on another journey.” “To Hangzhou or Huzhou?” “Hangzhou first. If Prefect Wang has already returned to his post, go on to Huzhou. You must find him wherever he is. And of course,” Hu added suddenly, “you can take A’zhu home at the same time.” “Very well. When do I leave?” “Within two or three days at most. As soon as I’ve made the arrangements here and written the letter.”

zh: 接头是跟古应春接头。第二天在怡情老二的香闺中，三个人又见了面，胡雪岩说了经过，问古应春，英国人肯不肯将枪炮、火药卖给这方面？“有啥不肯？他们是做生意，只要价钱谈得拢，什么都卖。”古应春问道，“你要些什么东西，我好去谈。”这下把胡雪岩难倒了，“这上面我一窍不通。”他说，“只要东西好就好。”“不光是东西好坏，还有数目多少。总要有个约数，才好去谈，譬如洋枪，应该多少支？”“总要一千支。”“一千支！”古应春笑道，“你当一千支是小数目？我看办团练，有五百支洋枪就蛮好了。还有，要不要请教习？洋枪不是人人会放的，不会用，容易坏，坏了怎么修，都要事先盘算过。”“应春兄，”胡雪岩拱拱手说，“你比我内行得太多了。索性你来弄个‘ 说帖’，岂不爽快？”
en: The arrangements were to be made with Gu Yingchun. The next day the three met again in Second Miss’s bedchamber at Yiqing House. Hu explained what they had discussed and asked whether the British would sell guns, cannon and powder to their side. “Why wouldn’t they? They are businessmen. If the price is right, they will sell anything. Tell me what you want, and I can negotiate.” This stumped Hu. “I know nothing about such things. So long as the goods are good, that is enough.” “Quality isn’t the only consideration. There is quantity too. I must have approximate figures before I can negotiate. How many foreign guns, for instance?” “A thousand, surely.” “A thousand!” Gu laughed. “Do you imagine that is a small number? Five hundred foreign guns would be quite a good supply for a militia force. And will you need instructors? Not everyone knows how to fire them. In inexperienced hands they are easily damaged. How will you repair them? All this must be considered beforehand.” Hu clasped his hands. “Brother Yingchun, you know far more about it than I do. Why don’t you draw up a memorandum yourself? That would settle everything.”

zh: 古应春慨然应诺，而且立刻功手。怡情老二亲自照料，移过“叫条子”用的笔砚来，磨浓了墨，却无纸可写，好在是草稿，不妨拿“局票”翻过来，将就着用。于是古应春一面提笔构思，一面过鸦片烟瘾，烟泡装上烟枪，枪嘴上接根橡皮管子，一直通到他嘴里。十六筒烟抽完，精神十足，文不加点，洋洋洒洒地写完，递到了胡雪岩手里。胡雪岩自己不能动笔，看却会看，不但会看，而且目光锐利，象这些“说帖”，最要紧的是简洁，要几句话就能把那些大官儿说动心，才是上品。古应春的笔下很来得，但流畅有余，不免枝蔓，他把洋枪、火药的好处，源源本本谈起，好虽好，看来却有些吃力。胡雪岩心想，这个说帖，王有龄、赵景贤一定会看完，但递到黄宗汉手中，他有没有看完的耐心，就难说了。
en: Gu readily agreed and began at once. Second Miss personally brought over the brush and inkstone used to write invitations to courtesans and ground a rich supply of ink. There was no blank paper, but since this was only a draft, the backs of the invitation slips would serve. Gu composed with his brush while indulging his opium habit. The prepared pellets were put into the pipe, with a rubber tube attached to the mouthpiece and reaching his lips. After sixteen pipefuls, he was in excellent spirits. His prose flowed freely, without a correction, and he handed the finished draft to Hu. Hu could not compose such a document himself, but he could read it—and judge it shrewdly. A memorandum of this kind had above all to be concise. The best would move a high official with a few sentences. Gu wrote fluently, but fluency had carried him into unnecessary elaboration. He explained the merits of foreign guns and gunpowder from their beginnings. The exposition was good, but somewhat laborious to read. Wang Youling and Zhao Jingxian would certainly finish it, Hu thought. Whether Huang Zonghan would have the patience was another question.

zh: “高明之至！”胡雪岩先声色不动地把说帖递给尤五。“我不必看了。”尤五笑道，“看也是白看。”“雪岩兄，”古应春接口问道：“我是急就章，有不妥的地方你尽管说。”“好极了！不过，应春兄，对外行不好说内行话，说了，人家也不懂。我看，前面这一段，有些地方要割爱。““我懂！”古应春点点头，“现在谈洋务，都是些闭门造车，自说自话蒙人的玩意。那些谈枪、炮怎么样制造的道理，说句实话，也真没有几个人懂，我可以把它删节。删归删、添归添，你看，哪里还可以多说两句？““很好了。还有些地方不说也可以。”这显然是客气话，古应春便说：“我这个人做事，不做则已，一做一定要把它做好，何况是自己人，尽请直言。”“既如此，我说出来请你斟酌，第一，说道光年间，‘英、法犯我，不幸丧师，症结所在，厥为刀矛不敌火器’，这句话一针见血，不过还可以着力说两句。”“对！我自己也有这么个想法。”
en: “Excellent!” Hu said, keeping his expression unchanged as he passed the memorandum to You. “There’s no need for me to read it,” You said with a laugh. “I wouldn’t get anything out of it.” “Brother Xueyan,” Gu put in, “this was written in haste. If anything is unsuitable, please say so.” “It is very good. Only, Brother Yingchun, you cannot talk to outsiders in the language of an expert. They won’t understand. I think you may have to sacrifice some of the opening section.” “I understand.” Gu nodded. “So much talk of foreign affairs nowadays consists of people shutting themselves away and spinning their own tales to deceive others. To be frank, very few understand the principles behind the manufacture of guns and cannon. I can shorten those passages. But cutting is one thing and adding another. Where might I usefully say more?” “It is very good already. There are still places where you could say less.” Recognizing this as politeness, Gu replied, “When I undertake something, I mean to do it properly. Besides, we are among friends. Please speak plainly.” “Then let me offer this for your consideration. First, you say, ‘During the Daoguang reign, Britain and France attacked us, and our forces suffered defeat; the essential cause was that swords and spears could not withstand firearms.’ That goes straight to the point, but it could be emphasized further.” “Yes! I had the same thought.”

zh: “再有一层，应春兄，是不是可以加这么一段……”胡雪岩所建议增加的是，说英国人运到上海的洋枪、火药有限，卖了给官军，就没有货色再卖给洪军及各地其他人，所以这方面多买一支，那方面就少得一支，出入之间，要以双倍计算。换句话说，官军花一支枪的钱，等于买了两支枪。“你这个算法倒很精明，无奈不合实情。英国人的军械，来了一批又一批，源源不绝，不会有什么卖给这个，就不能再卖给那个的道理。”“是的。应春兄，这种情形，我清楚，你更清楚，不过做官的清楚，京里的皇上和军机大臣，更不会清楚。我们只要说得动听就是。”古应春看着尤五笑了，尤五的话，很爽直：“应春兄，这些花样，我的这位小爷叔最在行，你听他的，包定不错。”“好！”古应春说，“我都懂了。如果没有别的话，我今天带回去，改好誊正，再连洋行里的估价单，一起开来交给你。”
en: “There is another point, Brother Yingchun. Could you add a passage along these lines?” Hu proposed saying that the supply of British guns and powder arriving in Shanghai was limited. What was sold to government forces would no longer be available to Hong’s army or other parties elsewhere. Every additional gun bought by the government would therefore mean one fewer in hostile hands, a difference that should count double. In other words, the government would obtain the benefit of two guns for the price of one. “That is a clever calculation,” Gu said, “but unfortunately it does not fit the facts. British arms arrive in one shipment after another, without interruption. Selling to one customer does not prevent them from selling to another.” “Of course. I know that, and you know it better still. But officials do not, and the emperor and the grand councillors in Beijing know even less. All we need is an argument they will like to hear.” Gu looked at You and smiled. You spoke bluntly. “Brother Yingchun, my young uncle here is an expert at these devices. Follow his advice and you won’t go wrong.” “Very well,” Gu said. “I understand. If there is nothing else, I will take this home today, revise it and make a fair copy. I’ll bring it back with a quotation from the firm.”

zh: “慢来！”尤五插嘴问道：“估价单怎么开法？”“照例是二人回扣。”古应春答道：“如果要‘戴帽子’，我亦可以去说。”听他的口气，显然不主张浮报价款的“戴帽子”。胡雪岩也觉得一方面不能叫洋人看不起，另一方面对浙江官方要建立信用，不宜在两成回扣以外，另出花样。“对！”尤五很诚恳地接受，“我原是怕你们疏忽，提一句。既然都曾想过，那就怎么样都是不错的了。”
en: “Wait a moment,” You interrupted. “How will the quotation be drawn up?” “The usual arrangement is a twenty-percent rebate,” Gu answered. “If you want the price padded, I can discuss that too.” His tone made it plain that he did not favor inflating the quoted price. Hu agreed. They must avoid earning the foreigners’ contempt, and they needed to establish their credit with the Zhejiang authorities. They ought not to invent further devices beyond the twenty-percent rebate. “Quite right,” You said sincerely. “I only mentioned it in case you had overlooked the matter. Since you have considered it, whatever you decide will be all right.”

zh: “不过，”古应春接下来问：“除了洋枪，还有大炮，要不要劝浙江买？”“这慢一点。浙江有个姓龚的，会造炮……”姓龚的福建人，名叫龚振麟，曾经做过嘉兴县的县丞，道光末年就在浙江主持“炮局”。从明朝中叶以来，一直在仿制的“红衣大将军炮”，都用生铁翻砂，龚振麟却发明了铸炮铁模，著成《图说》，还著了一本《枢机炮架新式图说》，在铸炮技术上，颇有改良。他的儿子名叫龚之棠，能得父传。父子二人、都很得浙江大吏的重用。“当然，打‘群子’的土造大炮，不及西洋的‘落地开花大炮’，但这话不能说！一说，炮局里的人当我们要敲他的饭碗，一定鸡蛋里挑骨头，多方挑剔，结果是连洋枪都不卖。”“雪岩兄，”古应春既感慨又佩服地，“你真正人情熟透，官场里的毛病，被你说尽了。”“官场、商场都一样！总而言之，‘同行相妒’，彼此能够不妒，什么事都可以成功！”
en: “But besides guns,” Gu continued, “there are cannon. Should we urge Zhejiang to buy those too?” “Let that wait. There is a man named Gong in Zhejiang who makes cannon.” Gong Zhenlin was a native of Fujian and had once served as deputy magistrate of Jiaxing. By the closing years of the Daoguang reign, he was directing Zhejiang’s cannon works. Since the middle of the Ming dynasty, the so-called Red-Robed General cannon had been copied by casting iron in sand molds. Gong had devised iron molds for casting cannon and had written an illustrated account of them. He had also written an Illustrated Account of a New Pivoted Gun Carriage, making significant improvements in cannon-making technology. His son, Gong Zhitang, had learned his craft from him. Both father and son were highly valued by Zhejiang’s senior officials. “Naturally, our locally made cannon firing clusters of shot cannot match the Western guns with shells that burst on impact. But we mustn’t say so! The men at the cannon works would think we were trying to take away their livelihood. They would find fault with everything, and we might end up unable to conclude even the purchase of guns.” “Brother Xueyan,” Gu said with mingled admiration and feeling, “you understand human affairs thoroughly. You have laid bare all the faults of official life.” “Business and official life are alike in that respect. People in the same trade envy one another. If only they could put envy aside, anything could be accomplished.”

zh: 古应春和尤五，都认为他这句话说得好，因此感情亦特别融洽。在怡情院中，浅斟低酌，谈了许多开展的计划，一直到午夜散席，约定第二天下午，仍旧在原处见面。古应春走了，尤五宿在怡情老二那里，因为还有事要谈，所以胡雪岩就在怡情院“借干铺”。尤五要谈的是，他这天中午，和胡雪岩分手以后，到怡情院重新见面以前，所得来的一个消息。听说，刘丽川跟英国人联系上了。夷场四周，英国人预备建筑围墙、不让官军进驻，也不准官军借道，但是英国人却预备开放陈家木桥，让刘丽川能够获得军火和粮食的接济。“照这样子，上海一年半载，不会光复。我们的丝生意，是不是做得下去？现在先要作个打算。”
en: Both Gu and You thought this well said, and their feelings toward one another grew warmer still. Over leisurely drinks at Yiqing House they discussed many plans for expanding their business. It was midnight before they parted, agreeing to meet there again the following afternoon. Gu left, while You stayed with Second Miss. Since there was more to discuss, Hu borrowed a bed at the house without engaging a companion. You had news acquired between their parting at noon and their meeting again at Yiqing House. Liu Lichuan had reportedly established contact with the British. The British intended to build a wall around the foreign settlement and allow neither government troops to be stationed inside nor government forces to pass through. Yet they planned to open Chenjia Wooden Bridge so that Liu could receive supplies of arms and food. “If that is so, Shanghai won’t be recovered for another six months or a year. Can we carry on our silk business? We had better consider it now.”

zh: “这倒要好好想一想。”胡雪岩提出疑问，“上海的关税，是两江的命脉，总不会一直让英国人张牙舞爪，一定有对付的办法。”“这也听说了。”尤五答道，“两江总督怡大人怊良，因为洋人助逆，早就预备禁止内地跟夷场通商。来源一断，我们在上海还有什么发展？”“这话分两方面来说，来源一断，货价必高，对我们有利，没有货色，货价再高也无用，对我们无利。”胡雪岩说，“生意还是可以照常做，只要对我们不利的这方面，能够避掉。”“怎么避呢？就是避不掉！”有个办怯，就是走私。以尤五在水路上的势力。呼应灵活，走私亦非难事，但犯法的勾当，胡雪岩不敢做，而且目前事事顺利，也犯不着去干犯法的勾当。就这一转念间，他把到口的话，缩了回去。“小爷叔，我想只有这么样，”尤五自己提出了一个办法：“尽量调动现款，就在上海收货，囤一段时间脱手。另外除了军火以外，有啥生意好做，我们再商量。顶好是我们漕帮弟兄能够一起出力的事，一则大家有口苦饭吃，二则也免得游手好闲去闯祸。”胡雪岩听出尤五的话中，对漕帮生计日窘，情有隐忧，既成知己，休戚相关，应该替他分优，于是问起松江漕帮的困难，看有什么办法好想？这一谈就谈得深了，直到天色微明。方始归寝。
en: “We must think carefully,” Hu said. “Shanghai’s customs revenue is the lifeblood of Liangjiang. They cannot let the British have their own way indefinitely. There must be a way of dealing with them.” “I have heard something about that too,” You replied. “Governor-General Yiliang has long been preparing to prohibit trade between the interior and the foreign settlement because the foreigners are helping the rebels. Once supplies are cut off, what prospects will we have in Shanghai?” “There are two sides to that. Cutting off supplies will raise prices, which helps us. But without goods, even the highest prices are useless to us. We can carry on business as usual if we can avoid the disadvantageous side.” “How can we avoid it? We can’t!” There was one way: smuggling. With You’s influence over the waterways and his responsive network, it would not be difficult. But Hu did not dare undertake something illegal. Everything was going well at present; there was no need to break the law. The thought passed through his mind, and he swallowed the words before uttering them. “Young Uncle, I can see only one course,” You said. “Raise as much ready cash as possible, buy goods already in Shanghai, hold them for a while and then sell. As for other business besides arms, we can discuss that too. Best of all would be something our grain-transport brothers could work at together. It would give everyone a hard-earned living and keep them from getting into trouble through idleness.” Hu heard the concealed anxiety behind these words about the brotherhood’s worsening livelihood. They were now close friends, sharing good fortune and bad; he ought to help You bear his worries. He asked about the difficulties facing the Songjiang brotherhood and what might be done. The discussion grew so absorbing that they did not go to bed until dawn.

zh: 一觉睡到近午时分，胡雪岩为怪情院一个“大姐”喊醒，说有客来。起床一看是陈世龙，递上一封信，说是王有龄专程派人送了来的。启封细看，才知道新城县抗粮滋事案，大功已成，嵇鹤龄不负所望，协同地方绅士，设计擒获首要各犯。已经解到杭州审讯法办。报告喜讯以外，接着便谈冬漕，因为上海失守，浙江的漕米海运。决定改由浏河出口。这一来便多了周折，所以必须提早一个月启运，连带也就要提早催征、王有龄得要赶回湖州。同时又因为上海失守的缘故，浙江人心惶惶，各地团练，都在加紧办理，湖州亦不例外，虽说有赵景贤主持其事，地方官守土有责，不能不问。所苦的是，海运局的差使还不能摆脱，分身乏术，希望胡雪岩无论如何回浙江一趟，他有许多事要当面商量。看完信，胡雪岩又高兴、又为难，而且还有些困惑，高兴的是新城建功，为难的是他亦分身乏术，困惑的是嵇鹤龄应有酬庸、却未见提起。怎么办？他定神想了想、决定回去一趟，但不能“空手而回”，有两件事，可以光为王有龄做好。想停当了他告诉陈世龙说：“你回去收拾行李，我们明天就走，阿珠也一起走。”
en: Hu slept until nearly noon, when one of the senior female attendants at Yiqing House woke him to say that he had a visitor. It was Chen Shilong, bringing a letter delivered by a special messenger from Wang Youling. Hu opened it and read carefully. The affair of the grain-tax disturbances in Xincheng had been brought to a successful conclusion. Ji Heling had fulfilled their expectations: working with local gentlemen, he had devised a plan to capture the principal offenders, who had been sent to Hangzhou for trial and punishment. After the good news came the question of the winter grain shipment. Because Shanghai had fallen, Zhejiang’s tribute rice would now be shipped out to sea through Liuhe. The extra complications meant starting a month early, and the collection of the grain tax would also have to be advanced. Wang needed to hurry back to Huzhou. Shanghai’s fall had caused alarm throughout Zhejiang, and militia organization was being pressed forward everywhere, Huzhou included. Although Zhao Jingxian was directing the work, the local official was responsible for the defense of his territory and could not leave it unattended. Yet Wang could not extricate himself from his duties at the Sea Transport Bureau and could not be in two places at once. He hoped that Hu would return to Zhejiang at all costs: there were many things they needed to discuss in person. Hu finished the letter pleased, troubled and puzzled. He was pleased by the success at Xincheng, troubled because he too had more than he could attend to, and puzzled because there was no mention of the reward Ji Heling deserved. What should he do? He collected his thoughts and decided to go back, but not empty-handed. There were two things he could first arrange for Wang. Having made up his mind, he told Chen, “Go back and pack. We leave tomorrow. A’zhu will come with us.”

zh: 接着，他匆匆漱洗，去找尤五商量，一谈漕米由浏河出口，尤五皱着眉说：“这麻烦大了！”“怎么呢？”“浏河在嘉定北面……”“啊！”胡雪岩失声而呼，漕米驶运到浏河，由青浦、嘉定这一条路走，是不可能了。“那么，该怎么走呢？”“要兜圈子！”尤五蘸青茶在桌上画出路线：“从嘉兴往北，由吴江，昆山、太仓到浏河。”“这真是兜了个大圈子。”胡雪岩又问，“太仓是不是靠近嘉定？”“是啊，太仓在嘉定西北，四五十里路。”说着，他深深看了胡雪岩一眼，意思是要当心周立春劫漕米。胡雪岩心里明白，灵机一动，笑嘻嘻地说道：“尤五哥，你的生意来了，靠交情卖铜钿，浙江冬漕，最后到训河那段路，归你包运好不好？”
en: He hurried through his washing and went to consult You. At the mention of sending the tribute rice out through Liuhe, You frowned. “That will cause a great deal of trouble.” “Why?” “Liuhe lies north of Jiading.” “Ah!” Hu exclaimed. Sending the grain boats to Liuhe by way of Qingpu and Jiading would be impossible. “Then which way can they go?” “They must make a detour.” Dipping a finger in clear tea, You traced the route on the table. “North from Jiaxing, through Wujiang, Kunshan and Taicang to Liuhe.” “That is a considerable detour. Is Taicang near Jiading?” “Yes, forty or fifty li northwest of it.” You gave Hu a significant look: they must beware of Zhou Lichun seizing the grain. Hu understood. An idea struck him, and he smiled. “Brother You, here is business for you. Turn your connections into money! How would you like the contract to carry Zhejiang’s winter tribute grain over the final stretch to Liuhe?”

zh: 这是顺理成章，极妙的事，但尤五因为来之太易，反有天下哪有这种好事的感觉，一时竟茫然不知所答。“怎么样？”胡雪岩催促着说，“这件事我有把握，完全可以作主，只等你一句话，事情就算定局。”“不晓得‘那方面’头不买我的帐？”尤五踌躇着说。出入关系，就在这一点上，所谓“靠交情，卖铜钿”也就是这一点，胡雪岩说道：“尤五哥，别的我都可以替你出主意，这方面要你自己才有数，我不便说什么！”“是的。”尤五深深点头。“这要我自己定主意。说实话，既然答应下来，要有肩胛，不能做连累你和王知府的荒唐事。这样，为求稳当，我只能暂且答应你。好在日子也还早，我托人跟‘圈吉’去打个招呼看看，如果口气不妙，我立刻通知你，只当没有说过这回事。你看怎么样？”“你怎么说，怎么说。我们假定事在必成，先商量商量怎么个办法。”于是议定浙江清船到吴江，归尤五接驳转运，到浏河海口为止。因为包运要担风险，水脚自然不能照常例计算。胡雪岩答应为他力争，多一个好一个。
en: It was a natural and excellent proposal. Yet it had come so easily that You could scarcely believe such good fortune existed; for a moment he did not know what to say. “Well?” Hu urged. “I am confident about this. I can settle it myself. One word from you, and it is arranged.” “I don’t know whether the other side will honor my connections,” You said hesitantly. That was the decisive point, the very basis of turning friendship into money. “Brother You,” Hu replied, “I can advise you on everything else. But only you can judge that. I cannot speak for you.” “Yes.” You nodded solemnly. “That is for me to decide. If I undertake it, I must shoulder the responsibility. I cannot do anything foolish that would involve you and Prefect Wang in trouble. To be safe, I can only agree provisionally. There is still time. I’ll send someone to sound out our friend Zhou. If his response is unfavorable, I’ll notify you at once, and we will treat the whole proposal as though it had never been made. What do you think?” “Whatever you say. Let us assume it will succeed and first discuss the arrangements.” They agreed that, once Zhejiang’s grain boats reached Wujiang, You would take over the cargo and carry it onward to the sea outlet at Liuhe. Since the contract involved risk, the freight rate could not follow the ordinary scale. Hu promised to argue for the best possible terms: every extra payment would help.

zh: 谈完了一件谈第二件，这要去找古应春、胡雪岩估计情势，浙江当道不但一定会买洋枪，而且因为上海失守，人心惶惶，防务亟待加强，所以对洋枪的需要，会倍感急迫。看准了这一点，不妨双管齐下，一面带说帖回去，劝浙江当道大批购买，一面带着现货回杭州，如果团练不用洋枪，就劝王有龄买了，供他的亲军小队使用。找到古应春家，只见他正衣冠整齐地，顶备到恰情院赴约。等胡雪岩说明来意，古应春想了一下问道：“你想要买多少支？”“先买两百支。”胡雪岩说，“我带了一万两银子在身上。”“两百支，有现货。你怎么运法？”古应春提醒他说，“运军械，要有公事，不然关卡上一定会被扣。”“是的。我跟尤五哥商量好了，由上海运到松江，不会有麻烦。我一到杭州。立刻就请了公事迎上来接货，这样在日子上就不会有耽搁了。”“好！我此刻就陪你去看洋人，当面议价。”说着，古应春拉了胡雪岩就走。
en: With the first matter settled, Hu turned to the second, which required a visit to Gu. From his assessment of the situation, the Zhejiang authorities would certainly buy foreign guns. Indeed, the alarm caused by Shanghai’s fall and the urgent need to strengthen defenses would make their demand especially pressing. He could therefore proceed on two fronts: take the memorandum back and urge a large official purchase, while also bringing guns ready for use to Hangzhou. If the militia did not buy them, he could persuade Wang to purchase them for his personal guard detachment. When Hu reached Gu’s house, he found him dressed and ready for their appointment at Yiqing House. After hearing Hu’s purpose, Gu considered for a moment and asked, “How many do you want?” “Two hundred to begin with. I have ten thousand taels with me.” “There are two hundred in stock. How will you transport them? You need official papers to move arms, or they are certain to be detained at a checkpoint.” “Yes. I have discussed it with Brother You. Getting them from Shanghai to Songjiang will cause no trouble. As soon as I reach Hangzhou, I’ll obtain the official documents and send to meet the shipment. That will avoid any delay.” “Good! I’ll take you to see the foreigner now, and we can negotiate the price in person.” He took Hu by the arm and started out.

zh: “慢点，慢点！”胡雪岩怯意地笑着，“跟洋人打交道，我还是第一回……”“你怕什么？”古应春打断他的话说，“洋人也是人，又不是野人生番，文明得很。”“不是说野蛮、文明，是有些啥洋规矩？你先说给我听听，省得我出洋相。”“这一时无从谈起。”古应春说，“中国人作揖，洋人握手，握右手。到屋子里要脱帽。洋人重堂客，回头你看见洋婆子要站起来，那个哈德逊太太很好客，最喜欢跟中国人问长问短，洋人的规矩是不大重男女大防的，你不必诧异。““这倒好，”胡雪岩笑道，“跟我们尤家那位七姑奶奶一样。”“你说谁？”“不相干的笑话，你不必理我。”胡雪岩摇摇手说，“我们走吧！”
en: “Wait, wait!” Hu said with a nervous smile. “This is my first time dealing with foreigners.” “What are you afraid of?” Gu interrupted. “Foreigners are human too. They are not wild savages. They are quite civilized.” “I don’t mean whether they are savage or civilized. What foreign rules of conduct should I know? Tell me beforehand so I don’t make a fool of myself.” “There is scarcely time to explain everything. We clasp our hands and bow; they shake hands—the right hand. Take off your hat indoors. They show respect to women, so stand when you see a foreign lady. Mrs Hudson is very hospitable and likes to ask Chinese visitors all sorts of questions. Their customs do not insist on a strict separation between men and women. Don’t be surprised.” “That sounds pleasant,” Hu said, laughing. “Like the Seventh Lady in the You household.” “Who do you mean?” “An irrelevant joke. Never mind me.” Hu waved it aside. “Let’s go.”

zh: 于是两乘肩舆，到了泥城桥一座小洋房，下轿投刺，被延入客厅，穿蓝布大褂的听差，也不奉茶，也不敬烟，关上房门就走了。隔不多久，靠里的一道门开启，长了满脸黄胡子的哈德逊大踏步走了出来。胡雪岩已打定主意，亦步亦趋跟着古应春，看他起身，他亦起身，看他握手，他亦握手，只有古应春跟洋人谈话时，他只能看他们脸上的表情。表情很不好，洋人只管耸肩摊手，而古应春大有恼怒之色，然后声音慢慢地高了，显然起了争执。“岂有此理！”古应春转过脸来，怒气冲冲地对胡雪岩说，“他明明跟我说过，贸易就是贸易，只要有钱，他什么能卖的东西都愿意卖，现在倒又翻悔了，说跟长毛有协议，卖了给他们就不能再卖给官军。我问他以前为什么不说，他说是他们领事最近才通知的。又说，他们也跟中国人一样，行动要受官府约束，所以身不由主。你说气人不气人？”“慢来！”胡雪岩问道：“什么叫协议，是不是条约的意思？”“大致就是这意思。”“那就不对了，朝廷跟英国人订了商约，开五口通商，反而我们不能跟他通商，朝廷讨伐的叛逆，倒能够跟他通商。这是啥道理！”
en: Two sedan chairs took them to a small Western house at Nicheng Bridge. They alighted, sent in their visiting cards and were shown into the drawing room. The servant, dressed in a long blue cotton gown, offered neither tea nor tobacco; he simply closed the door and went away. Before long an inner door opened, and Hudson, his face covered in a yellow beard, strode in. Hu had resolved to copy Gu exactly. When Gu rose, he rose; when Gu shook hands, he shook hands. But when conversation began, Hu could do nothing except watch their expressions. Those expressions were far from reassuring. The foreigner kept shrugging and spreading his hands, while Gu looked increasingly angry. Their voices gradually rose: plainly they were arguing. “Outrageous!” Gu turned to Hu in fury. “He told me clearly that business was business: if a customer had money, he would sell anything he was able to sell. Now he goes back on it. He says he has an agreement with the Long-Haired rebels and cannot sell to government troops after selling to them. I asked why he hadn’t said so before. He claims his consul only recently informed him of it. He says they are subject to their authorities just as we are to ours and cannot act as they please. Isn’t that infuriating?” “Wait,” Hu said. “What does he mean by an agreement? Something like a treaty?” “Roughly speaking, yes.” “Then it makes no sense. Our government made a commercial treaty with Britain, opening five ports to trade. Yet we cannot trade with him, while rebels whom our government is fighting can! What sort of reasoning is that?”

zh: 古应春大喜，“不错，不错。说得真有道理！等我问他。”于是古应春转脸跟哈德逊办交涉，胡雪岩虽然听不懂意思，却听得出语气，看得出神色，古应春一派理直气壮的声音，而哈德逊似乎有些词穷了。到最后只见洋人点头，古应春含笑，向胡雪岩说道：“成功了！他答应跟他们领事去申诉。看样子未必有什么协议，只因为我们的生意小，长毛的生意大，伯贪小失大而已。”“请你告诉他，眼前我们的生意小，将来生意会很大，眼光要放远些，在目前留些交情，将来才有见面的余地。”古应春便把他的话译了过去，洋人不断颔首，同时也不断看着胡雪岩，显然是心许其言。“雪岩兄，”古应春说：“他说，你的话很有意味，要交你一个朋友，想请你去喝杯酒。问你的意思怎么样？”“当然，应该叙叙，归我们做东好了。”“那倒不必。让他做东好了。等生意谈妥，我们再回请。”
en: Gu was delighted. “Exactly! That is a very good argument. Let me put it to him.” He turned back to negotiate. Hu could not understand the words, but he could hear the tone and read the expressions. Gu spoke with the confidence of a man who had right on his side; Hudson seemed at a loss for an answer. At last the foreigner nodded, and Gu turned to Hu with a smile. “We have done it! He has agreed to take the matter up with his consul. I suspect there may be no agreement at all. Our order is small and the rebels’ orders are large; he is merely afraid of losing the greater profit for the smaller.” “Tell him that our business is small now but will be large in the future. He should take the long view. If he cultivates our friendship today, we can continue dealing with him tomorrow.” Gu translated. Hudson nodded repeatedly and kept looking at Hu, plainly approving of what he had said. “Brother Xueyan, he finds your remarks very interesting and would like to make a friend of you. He wants to invite you for a drink. What do you say?” “Of course. We should get better acquainted. Let us be the hosts.” “There is no need. Let him entertain us this time. We can return the invitation once the business is settled.”

zh: 于是，等古应春转达了接受邀请的答复，哈德逊到屋角将一条在中国犯禁的“明黄”色丝绦一拉，外面叮叮当当的响了起来，接着便见原来的那个听差推门而入，这让胡雪岩学了个乖，洋人招呼听差，是打铃不是拉长了声音喊：“来呀！”哈德逊吩咐听差，是准备马车，亲自拉缰，把他们两人载到一家外国酒店，入门一看，胡雪岩觉得有些头晕，四面镜子，映出无数人影、灯烛、桌椅，赶紧顺手扶住一张椅子，立定了脚再说。“就是这里吧！”古应春喊住哈德逊，各拉一张椅子坐下来。于是胡雪岩也拉开椅子坐下，一抬眼，恰好看见镜子中出现的丽影，转脸来望，见是个金发碧眼的美女，真正是雪肤花貌，腰如一捻，露出一嘴雪白的牙齿，笑着在问话。于是哈德逊嘱咐了几句，那女侍转身走了。胡雪岩不便盯着她的背影看，只望着镜子。西洋女人见得还不多，这一望，眼睛使舍不得离开镜子，看到那刚健婀娜的行路姿态，不由得想起穿着“花盆底”的旗下大姑娘，一摇三摆的样子，觉得各擅胜场，都比三寸金莲、走路讲究裙幅不动的汉人妇女来得中看。正在这样想着，镜中的丽影又出现了，她手托银盘，盘中一瓶颜色象竹叶青的酒，三只水晶杯，又有一瓶凉水。摆设停当，哈德逊取了三块银洋，放在银盘里。
en: When Gu conveyed their acceptance, Hudson went to a corner and pulled a silk bell cord in the bright yellow reserved for imperial use in China. A jangling sounded outside, and the servant returned. Hu learned something: foreigners summoned servants by ringing a bell instead of drawing out a loud cry of “Come!” Hudson ordered the carriage, took the reins himself and drove them to a Western drinking establishment. As Hu entered, he felt dizzy. Mirrors on every side multiplied the people, lamps, tables and chairs without end. He quickly grasped a chair and steadied himself. “Let’s sit here,” Gu called to Hudson, and each drew up a chair. Hu sat down too. Looking up, he caught the reflection of a beautiful figure in a mirror. He turned and saw a blonde, blue-eyed woman with a snow-white complexion, lovely features and a slender waist. Her smile revealed white teeth as she asked a question. Hudson gave her an order, and she turned away. Hu could hardly stare openly after her, so he watched her in the mirror. He had seen few Western women, and now found it difficult to take his eyes from the reflection. Her vigorous yet graceful stride reminded him of the swaying walk of young Manchu women in their flowerpot-soled shoes. Each had its own charm; both seemed more attractive to him than Han women with tiny bound feet, whose ideal was to walk without disturbing the folds of their skirts. While he was thinking this, the waitress reappeared in the mirror carrying a silver tray. On it were a bottle of liquor resembling Bamboo Leaf Green in color, three crystal glasses and a bottle of cold water. Once she had set them down, Hudson placed three silver dollars on the tray.

zh: “这酒也不便宜。”胡雪岩说，“一块银洋七钱二，三块银洋就合到二两一钱多银子。”“是啊！运费贵。”古应春答了他一句，帮着哈德逊倒酒，又加上凉水，然后彼此举一举杯。“怎么？”胡雪岩问：“这就吃了？有酒无肴！”“洋盘！”古应春用夷场中新近流行的谚语笑他，“洋人吃酒，没有菜的。”“这我倒还是第一回。”胡雪岩喝了一口，酒味倒还不坏，但加了水，觉得劲道不够，便又把杯子放下了。“我们谈生意吧！”古应春说了一声，跟哈德逊去交谈，然后又问胡雪岩说，“他问你货色什么时候要？”“最多三天就要起运。”“那价钱就不同了。”古应春说，“有一批货色，他已经答应了镇江一个姓罗的长毛，你要可以先给你，要三十两银子一支。如果你肯等半个月，他另有一批货色从英国运到，只要二十两一支。““三十两就三十两。货色要好。”
en: “This liquor isn’t cheap,” Hu remarked. “A silver dollar is worth seven qian and two fen. Three dollars come to more than two taels and one qian.” “Yes, freight is expensive,” Gu replied. He helped Hudson pour the liquor and add cold water; then they raised their glasses to one another. “What?” Hu asked. “We drink now? Wine without dishes?” “A novice in foreign ways!” Gu teased him with a new expression current in the settlement. “Foreigners drink without food.” “Well, that is a first for me.” Hu took a sip. The flavor was not bad, but diluted with water it lacked strength. He put down the glass. “Let’s talk business,” Gu said. After speaking with Hudson, he turned back. “He asks when you need the goods.” “They must be dispatched within three days at most.” “Then the price will be different. He has a shipment already promised to a rebel named Luo at Zhenjiang. He can let you have it first, but it will be thirty taels a gun. If you can wait half a month, another shipment will arrive from Britain, and those would be only twenty taels each.” “Thirty it is. The goods must be good.”

zh: 古应春点点头，又跟哈德逊去说。就这样由他居间口译，很快地谈妥了一切细节，两百支枪，一万发子药，总价一万一千两银子，二八回扣，实收八千八百两。另外由哈德逊派一名“铜匠”随货到浙江去照料，要二百两银子的酬劳。“贷款我带在身上，是不是此刻就交？”“不必。”古应春说，“明天到他洋行里去办手续。”“那就托你了。”胡雪岩取出银票，交了过去，“这里一万两，多的是你的。”“用不着。”古应春急忙摇手，“大家一起做，回扣列入公帐，将来再说。”“这话也对。那么，多的一千两算存在你的手里好了。”
en: Gu nodded and spoke to Hudson again. With him interpreting between them, they soon settled every detail: two hundred guns and ten thousand rounds of ammunition, at a total price of eleven thousand taels. After a twenty-percent rebate, the sum payable was eight thousand eight hundred. Hudson would also send a gunsmith with the shipment to Zhejiang to attend to the weapons, for a fee of two hundred taels. “I have the money with me. Shall I pay now?” “No need,” Gu replied. “We can complete the formalities at his firm tomorrow.” “Then I’ll leave it to you.” Hu took out his banknotes and handed them over. “Here are ten thousand taels. The surplus is yours.” “There is no need for that!” Gu hastily waved the suggestion aside. “We are all in this together. The rebate goes into our common accounts. We can settle our shares later.” “Quite right. Then consider the remaining thousand taels a deposit you are holding for me.”

zh: 古应春点点头，指着银票又跟哈德逊去谈，只见洋人笑容满面，很快的说了好些话，据古应春传译，哈德逊认为跟胡雪岩做生意，很痛快，他要额外送一支最新式的“后膛七响”，以表敬意。“ 请你替我说，谢谢！”胡雪岩又说，“再请你问问他，那种什么”后膛七响‘，可以不可以卖几支给我？我要带回去送人。“这有些困难，哈德逊在中国好几年，深知贪小便宜的人多，留着几支好枪要用来应酬人情，不肯出售。然而最后哈德逊却又让步了，愿意匀出两支来卖给胡雪岩，价钱是每支一百五十两银子，据他说，完全是照成本出让。每支枪另配一百粒子药，也是白送。
en: Gu nodded, pointed to the notes and spoke to Hudson, whose face broke into a broad smile. He said a great deal very quickly. According to Gu, Hudson found doing business with Hu so agreeable that he wished to present him with one of the latest breech-loading, seven-shot guns as an additional mark of esteem. “Please thank him for me,” Hu said. “And ask whether he could sell me a few of those—what are they called?—seven-shot breech-loaders. I should like to take some home as gifts.” This was less easy. Hudson had spent several years in China and knew how fond many people were of small favors. He was keeping a few fine guns for cultivating useful relationships and did not want to sell them. In the end, however, he yielded and agreed to spare two for Hu, at one hundred and fifty taels apiece, which he said was exactly the cost price. Each would come with a hundred rounds of ammunition, also given free.

zh: 做了额外的这笔小交易，哈德逊要开一瓶香摈酒庆祝。古应春心想，胡雪岩对那种带点酸味的淡酒，未见得会感兴趣，而开一瓶香摈很贵，让哈德逊破费还是小事，回头胡雪岩端起杯子一喝，皱眉摇头，浅尝即止，那就是件很不礼貌的事，不如辞谢了的好。于是他告诉哈德逊，说胡雪岩喝不惯洋酒，不能领受他的好意，表示抱歉，哈德逊厦问，胡雪岩是不是不会喝酒？及至听说他的酒量很好时，哈德逊使表示奇怪，说桌上那瓶酒，来自苏格兰，不但是最有名的牌子，而且窖藏甚久，为何胡雪岩不喝？又说，他跟好些中国人有过交往，凡是会喝酒的，都欣赏苏格兰的酒，何以胡雪岩独异？接着又表示，如果胡雪岩不介意，他很想知道其中的缘故。古应春想敷衍一下，就算过去。倒是胡雪岩看哈德逊不断指着酒瓶和他的酒杯。滔滔不绝地在说话，猜到是谈杯中物，便自己先问起此事。古应春自然照实回答。“饮食一道，萝卜、青菜，各人自爱，好象女人一样，情人眼里出西施，没有什么道理好讲的。”古应春把他这一段话译给哈德逊听，洋人大点其头，说饮食没有道理好讲，这就是道理。接着又说，外国酒种类很多，胡雪岩不喜欢英国酒，也许喜欢法国的白兰地，于是招一招手把那女侍叫了过来，指明要一种名牌的白兰地。
en: To celebrate this additional little transaction, Hudson proposed opening a bottle of champagne. Gu doubted that Hu would care for a light wine with a somewhat sour taste. Champagne was expensive, but putting Hudson to expense was the lesser concern. If Hu tasted it, frowned, shook his head and refused another sip, that would be distinctly rude. Better to decline. He therefore apologized on Hu’s behalf, saying that Hu was unaccustomed to foreign liquor and could not accept the kind offer. Hudson asked in return whether Hu was unable to drink. On learning that he had a considerable capacity, Hudson was astonished. The bottle on the table came from Scotland, he said; it was not only a celebrated brand but had been aged for a long time. Why would Hu not drink it? He knew many Chinese, and all who enjoyed liquor appreciated Scotch. What made Hu different? If Hu did not mind, he would very much like to know. Gu meant to give an evasive answer and let the matter pass. But Hu saw Hudson repeatedly indicating the bottle and his glass while talking at length. Guessing the subject, he asked about it, and Gu naturally told him the truth. “In eating and drinking, one man likes radishes and another likes greens. It is like women: to a lover, his beloved is as beautiful as Xi Shi. There is no explaining tastes.” Gu translated this, and Hudson nodded emphatically. Saying that tastes could not be explained was itself an explanation. There were many kinds of foreign liquor, he added. If Hu did not like British liquor, perhaps he would enjoy French brandy. He beckoned to the waitress and named a particular celebrated brand.

zh: 喝这种酒又是一种杯子，矮脚敞口大肚子，但酒例得不多，也不掺水。哈德逊通过古应春，教胡雪岩喝这种酒的方法，说要双手台捧酒杯，慢慢摇晃，等手心里的热气，传入酒中，香味自发，便益觉醇美。胡雪岩如法炮制，试一试果如其言。哈德逊告诉古应春说，他终于找到了一种为胡雪岩所喜爱的酒，觉得很高兴。接着便谈白兰地的制法，由采撷葡萄到装瓶出售，讲碍非常详细。最后指着标贴纸上的一个洋字，读出它的译名叫“可涅克”，说选白兰地，一定要注意这个字，它是地名，法国出酒最好的地方。“我懂了！”胡雪岩对古应春说，“好比中国的黄酒一样，一定要‘绍兴’才道地。”“对，就是这意思。”
en: Brandy required a different glass: short-stemmed, broad-mouthed and round-bowled. Only a little was poured, without water. Through Gu, Hudson taught Hu how to drink it. He should cradle the glass in both hands and swirl it gently; as warmth from his palms entered the liquor, its fragrance would rise and its mellow flavor become more apparent. Hu followed these directions and found them justified. Hudson told Gu how pleased he was to have found a liquor Hu enjoyed. He then described brandy-making in great detail, from harvesting grapes to bottling the finished drink. Finally, he pointed to a word on the label and pronounced it: “Cognac.” When choosing brandy, he said, one should always look for this word. It was a place-name, the finest liquor-producing district in France. “I understand!” Hu told Gu. “Just like our yellow wine: it has to be Shaoxing to be authentic.” “Exactly.”

zh: “现在……”哈德逊接着便跟古应春说，他的洋行，刚刚取得这种法国酒的代理权，希望胡雪岩为他介绍买卖。“ 原来他是推销货色！”胡雪岩笑道，“怪不得这么起劲。不过我不懂，什么叫‘代理权’？”“就是归他包卖。”古应春为他解释，“这种俩在我们中华土地上，归他总经销，坐抽水子，这就叫代理权。“胡雪岩立刻就懂了，这种坐享其成的事，完全要靠信誉，牌号响，信用好，货色销得出去，货款收得进来，到时候结帐，不久分文，人家才肯赋予代理权。他心里在想，自己也大可这么做，不过那是将来的事，眼前怎么样也谈不到此，所以不再往下说了。
en: “Now…” Hudson went on to tell Gu that his firm had just obtained the agency for this French liquor, and he hoped Hu would introduce customers. “So he is promoting his merchandise!” Hu laughed. “No wonder he is so enthusiastic. But I don’t understand: what does an agency mean?” “He has the exclusive right to sell it,” Gu explained. “He is the general distributor of this liquor in China and takes a commission on the sales. That is what an agency means.” Hu understood at once. Such a business, earning its return from arranging sales, depended entirely on reputation and credit. A firm needed a respected name, sound credit, the ability to sell the goods and collect payment, and accounts settled punctually without a penny left owing. Only then would another company grant it an agency. He thought he might very well do the same himself. But that was for the future, beyond any immediate prospect, so he did not pursue the subject.

zh: 酒味甚美，只是有酒无肴，胡雪岩还不习惯这样的饮酒方式，所以喝得不多，但为了酬答雅意，也为了馈赠所需，他决定买五箱白兰地带回去。哈德逊也很会做生意，马上又给他一个很优惠的折扣，他的目的是在推广。杭州是浙江省城，除了总督，各式各样的衙门都有，又是运河起点，商业相当繁盛，这个码头在哈德逊看，是可以有所作为的，他希望得到胡雪岩的助力，能够把他所代理的各种洋货，推销到杭州。这番意思经由古应春表达以后，胡雪岩自然欢迎，但他跟古应春说了实话，他官商两方面，缠在手里的事情实在太多，一时无法给哈德逊任何确实的答复，看这话是如何说法？“那就直接回头他！”这里的“回头”是辞谢的意思，胡雪岩却又觉得这是个机会，弃之可惜，最好是拖延着，要能让哈德逊不找别人，为他保留着这个机会。脑筋一动，想到了一番话：“你这样跟他说，本来我马上可以答应他，为他在杭州策划，但目前局势不稳，上海到杭州的路会断，货源不继，变成白贴开销。等局势稍微稳定下来，我马上替他动手。”哈德逊认为他的看法很稳健，同意等一等再说，不过他要求胡雪岩在杭州先替他看看洋货的行情，预作准备，将来有任何代理承销的机会，答应让胡雪岩优先承揽。
en: The brandy tasted excellent, but Hu was still unused to drinking without food and took little. To acknowledge Hudson’s hospitality, and to supply himself with gifts, he decided to buy five cases to take home. Hudson was a shrewd businessman too and immediately offered a generous discount. His aim was to promote the product. Hangzhou was Zhejiang’s provincial capital, with every kind of government office except that of a governor-general. It was also the starting point of the canal and a flourishing commercial center. Hudson saw considerable potential in the port and hoped Hu would help sell there the various foreign goods for which his firm held agencies. When Gu explained this, Hu naturally welcomed the proposal. But he spoke frankly to Gu: he already had far too much official and commercial business on his hands to give Hudson a definite answer. How should they put that? “Then simply turn him down.” Hu felt, however, that this was an opportunity too valuable to discard. Better to delay in such a way that Hudson would keep the opportunity for him instead of approaching someone else. An idea occurred to him. “Tell him this: ordinarily I could agree at once to organize matters for him in Hangzhou. But conditions are unsettled. The route from Shanghai to Hangzhou may be cut, interrupting supplies and leaving us to pay expenses for nothing. As soon as the situation becomes a little more stable, I will get to work for him.” Hudson thought this a prudent judgment and agreed to wait. Meanwhile, he asked Hu to investigate the Hangzhou market for foreign goods and make preliminary preparations. He promised Hu the first opportunity to take up any future agency or distribution arrangement.

zh: 生意谈到这里为止，彼此都觉得很圆满。古、胡二人先起身告辞，安步当车，走回怡情院。一路走，一路谈，谈的却不是生意。胡雪岩问道：“怎么样？外国酒馆里的那个洋女人，算是啥名堂？”“卖酒的还有啥名堂！”古应春笑道，“你想她卖啥？”胡雪岩笑笑不答，不一会却又以抱憾的声音说：“可惜我不懂洋文。不然，跟她谈谈说说，一定是蛮有趣的一件事。”“我倒想不到，”古应春也笑了，“你会中意洋女人！”“女人总是女人，管她是华是洋，只要动人就好。”“慢慢来！”古应春说，“将来你在上海住长了，总有跟洋女人落个交情的时候。”
en: Their business discussions ended to everyone’s satisfaction. Gu and Hu took their leave and walked back to Yiqing House. They talked on the way, but no longer about business. “Tell me,” Hu asked, “what exactly is the position of that foreign woman in the drinking place?” “She sells liquor. What else?” Gu laughed. “What did you imagine she sold?” Hu smiled without answering. After a while he said regretfully, “It is a pity I don’t understand their language. Otherwise it would surely be interesting to talk with her.” “I wouldn’t have expected you to take a fancy to a foreign woman,” Gu said, laughing too. “A woman is a woman. Chinese or foreign makes no difference, so long as she is attractive.” “Give it time,” Gu replied. “Once you have lived in Shanghai longer, you will have opportunities to make friends with foreign women.”
